clue.text: Promptly gripped aluminium bar

indicators.note: gripped says one word holds the other inside it, as a hand clasps something

parts.note: promptly means soon, without delay
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Someone quickly grabs a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar, a room in a pub or the drinking place of a Wild West town.

clue.text: Volunteers to take tops from boxes

indicators.note: taking the top off a down entry means its first letter is removed

parts.note: coffers are strong boxes for valuables

explanation.surface: Helpers are asked to remove the lids from some crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take tops from' removes the first letter C from COFFERS. 'Volunteers' is a verb here, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to proffer it willingly, so volunteers is a verb meaning proffers.

clue.text: Tidy knight gobbled up!

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
gobbled up means eaten, consumed greedily

explanation.surface: A cry that a chess knight has been swallowed whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy something is to make it neat and orderly, a direct synonym as verbs.

clue.text: Irritates but doesn't start on joints

indicators.note: something that does not start loses its opening letter here

parts.note: rankles means irritates, festers in the mind

explanation.surface: Something annoys a person without kicking off a row in the body's joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops the first letter R from RANKLES.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint linking foot and leg, so ankles are joints.

clue.text: Help Fanny to exchange old coin

indicators.note: exchanging the places of letters means rearranging them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Assist a woman called Fanny in swapping an antique piece of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HELP and FANNY rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The British pre-decimal coin worth half of one penny was withdrawn in 1969, so it is an old coin.

clue.text: Mollusc deity has a temper

indicators.note: has means the god holds the other letters within itself

parts.note: a deity is a god
a strop is a fit of bad temper, British slang

explanation.surface: A god is in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' signals a container: the deity holds the rest. 'Temper' is a noun here, a fit of sulking in British slang, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails and slugs are gastropods, the largest class of molluscs.

clue.text: To put off tenancy payments, it's a discouragement

parts.note: to put off means to deter, dissuade
rent is what a tenant pays

explanation.surface: Charging rent to drive away tenants acts as a disincentive.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent is something that discourages action, so it is a discouragement.

clue.text: Father given part temporary release

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a role is a part played by an actor

explanation.surface: A dad is cast in a role and let out briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is the conditional, temporary release of a prisoner before the sentence ends.

clue.text: Ploughman at the helm

definitions.meaning: one who tills the soil, a farmer working the land
the bar used to steer a boat, held by whoever is steering

explanation.surface: A farmer who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller tills the land as a ploughman does, and is also the steering lever at a boat's helm.

clue.text: Grass found in dry environment

indicators.note: found in says the letters are tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some grass growing in an arid setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal grass grown for grain and whisky.

clue.text: Hinders the development of daring feats

definitions.meaning: to stunt growth is to hold it back
acrobatic or dangerous tricks performed to impress

explanation.surface: Doing dangerous tricks holds back one's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb for checking growth; the other is the noun for spectacular risky acts.

clue.text: Begin filling street with such a substance

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its interior once the outer letters are removed

parts.note: begin means start

explanation.surface: Start to cover a road with a sticky material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' keeps the interior of START by removing its first and last letters S and T. The definition points back to the street: a road is surfaced with this.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is the black, sticky substance used to surface roads.

clue.text: Settled in street surrounded by poverty

indicators.note: surrounded by means the street abbreviation is enclosed by the other word

parts.note: need is poverty, want

explanation.surface: Someone came to live on a road in a poor area.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that have nested have settled in a home, as people settle down.

clue.text: Bird in the mud

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird stuck in the mire.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Learning about ultraviolet in French gallery

indicators.note: about means the word for learning goes round the other letters

parts.note: lore is learning, traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Studying ultraviolet light at a Paris art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre is the great art museum in Paris, so a French gallery.

clue.text: Retailer drove off round back of station

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters encircle the final letter
off means the letters are out of order, to be rearranged
the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper drove away from the rear of the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' makes VEDOR from DROVE; 'round' puts N, the last letter of 'station', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is a seller, and a retailer is one who sells goods to the public.

clue.text: Small measure given to gaffer for carving, that's a relief

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measure, the width of a letter M
gaffer is British slang for boss, the person in charge

explanation.surface: A worker relieved to be given a tiny tool by the foreman for some woodwork.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER is British slang for a foreman or boss. 'that's a relief' completes the definition, describing carving with raised designs.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to carve or mould a raised design, which is relief work.

clue.text: Stitch certain to grip you French

indicators.note: to grip means the word for certain holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: sure means certain
tu is the French for you

explanation.surface: Someone is bound to hold onto a French person with a needle and thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture is a surgical stitch closing a wound.

clue.text: Painful injury seen right in the country

indicators.note: in means the letter for right sits inside the country's name

parts.note: Spain is the country here

explanation.surface: A nasty injury noticed correctly somewhere in the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a painful twisting injury to a joint's ligaments.

clue.text: Some mixture entering serving dish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a mixture going into a dish for serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep lidded bowl from which soup is served at the table.

clue.text: Master parking from street plan

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A graduate finds parking with a city chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A street plan is a chart of a town's roads.

clue.text: Associate with a biscuit

definitions.meaning: to mix socially, especially with important people

explanation.surface: Mingling socially over a cookie.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hobnob is a popular British oat biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb for mixing socially; the other is a British oaty cookie brand.

clue.text: Eager to go right, scattering grain

indicators.note: scattering means the letters are strewn into a different order

explanation.surface: A farmer keen to get going correctly, sowing seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means very keen and impatient to start.

clue.text: Hatches a scheme with prisoners outside part of the church

indicators.note: outside means the convicts go round the other piece

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
a spire is the pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Convicts plot an escape around the church steeple.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot in secret, so to hatch a scheme with others.
